name: Agri Sarthi
summary: An interactive crop-awareness experience that helps make early observation and field scouting easier to understand.
challenge: Crop information is often fragmented. The product question was how to give an observation a useful next step while keeping the experience approachable for farmers.
approach: I connected a botanical visual language, an animated product story and a local field notebook. Crop evidence is presented with source context; guided scouting and prepared advice help users record what they see.
features: Crop profile and guided scouting checklist
Observation notes saved locally in the browser
Downloadable field notes and clear local-data controls
Ten animated story scenes and interactive tour controls
scope: The public app is a working interface and crop-awareness concept. A trained disease model and live farm monitoring are not connected to this demo.
reflection: The strongest part of an AI product is often the step after a prediction: what someone understands, records and does next.
contribution: Interactive story, scouting flow and local field notebook.
outcome: Working browser prototype; no live disease model connected.

name: Suraksha One
summary: A smart-helmet concept and supervisor interface exploring clearer safety signals, worker status and emergency response.
challenge: Safety interfaces need to bring urgent information forward without making every sensor reading compete for attention.
approach: The web experience combines a helmet explorer, visual explanations and a telemetry dashboard. I used a clear hierarchy for gas, health and environment readings, with separate worker views and response controls.
features: Gas, temperature, heart-rate and SpO2 presentation
scope: The published web dashboard simulates its telemetry. It demonstrates the interface and system concept; it is not presented as a certified or field-validated safety system.
reflection: A safety dashboard should help a person decide what needs attention, not simply put more numbers on a screen.
contribution: 3D helmet experience, worker views and telemetry interface.
outcome: Interactive demo with simulated readings, not field validation.

name: MetroMaarg
summary: A metro travel prototype bringing route planning, ticket journeys and operational dashboards into one experience.
challenge: A journey crosses several decisions: which route to take, what the fare means and where the ticket lives. Those steps need a consistent interface.
approach: The repository combines React and TypeScript views with Supabase-backed services. Passenger flows cover routes and tickets, while administrator pages explore train status, analytics and QR generation.
features: Station selection, route options and fare presentation
Passenger account and ticket history views
Administrative train, analytics and QR interfaces
scope: This is an independent prototype, not an official metro service. Public source contains the application flows and backend functions; production transit integration is not claimed.
reflection: Designing both passenger and operator views makes the relationship between a simple screen and its underlying data much clearer.

name: Nexus AI Ops
summary: An agency operations prototype connecting content, briefs, campaign review and reporting with AI-assisted workflows.
challenge: Agency work passes through scattered briefs, content drafts, campaign updates and reports. The goal is a shared view of those steps with useful automation at the handoffs.
approach: A Next.js command center organizes the work. Gemini integration handles generation and analysis, while n8n workflow definitions connect status updates, content approvals, campaign alerts, briefs and weekly reporting.
features: Report generation and configurable webhook connections
scope: The repository supports demo data and fallback responses. Live AI and Slack/Notion automation depend on separately configured credentials and services.
reflection: Useful automation keeps its inputs, review points and outcomes visible. The interface is part of the system.
contribution: Agency dashboard, Gemini integration and n8n workflow definitions.
outcome: Demo mode works; live integrations require service configuration.

name: Resume Intelligence
summary: A document-analysis prototype combining PDF extraction, semantic retrieval and structured résumé-to-role comparisons.
challenge: A résumé workflow needs to preserve the evidence behind a summary so a reviewer can inspect it.
approach: The FastAPI application extracts PDF text, requests Gemini embeddings and queries Pinecone namespaces for job descriptions and candidate context. A dashboard presents the analysis and search workflow.
scope: An exploratory document-analysis tool requiring configured Gemini and Pinecone services. Its summaries and comparisons are intended to support human review.
reflection: An AI summary is more useful when a person can trace it back to the source material and make their own judgment.

name: QA Matrix
summary: An AI-assisted quality workflow exploring test planning, automation generation and failure analysis from requirements.
challenge: Requirements, test plans and failure reports can drift apart. This project explores how retrieval can keep their context connected.
approach: The repository brings together a FastAPI dashboard, Gemini integration, a vector-retrieval path and automation workflows. Its interfaces cover test matrices, generated scripts, failure analysis and API checks.
features: Automation generation for multiple test frameworks
API assertions and n8n workflow integration
scope: An AI-assisted developer-tool prototype. Generated tests and suggested fixes require review and execution; external AI and retrieval services need configuration.
reflection: Good test tooling should make assumptions visible and make it easier to challenge the result.

name: VEENA Rover
summary: A disaster-response rover project exploring person detection, environmental sensing and operator communication.
challenge: Rescue-oriented robotics brings computer vision into difficult physical conditions, where sensing, movement and operator feedback need to work together.
approach: My project work connects a Raspberry Pi computer-vision pipeline with an ESP32/ESP32-CAM hardware system, environmental sensors, motor control and Wi-Fi communication.
features: Ultrasonic, gas, flame and temperature sensing
Operator alerts and two-way communication concept
scope: A hardware prototype exploring sensing, computer vision and operator communication. A public source repository and a detailed performance report are not available here yet.
reflection: Working with hardware makes constraints tangible: compute, power, communication and human response all matter.
